$comment: The vocabulary every idiom's topology is written in. One list, in one
place: sixty idiom files each naming module kinds in their own words would
be sixty chances to write 'envelope' where the checker expects 'Envelope
generator', and the failure would be a silently unmatched requirement --
that is, an idiom that passes because nothing could test it.
`tags` are Rack's own canonical module tags, which the inventory carries
for every installed module including third-party ones. `ports` are the
port roles the cartographer assigns. An idiom refers to a role by name;
idiom_check.py resolves it here and nowhere else.
A module matches a role if it carries ANY of the role's tags. A port
matches if its role is in `ports`, or if its silkscreen label matches one
of `labels` -- the label fallback exists because a module we have not
cartographed has no port roles at all, and refusing to check those patches
would quietly exempt exactly the modules most likely to be miswired.

`fan_in` marks a role whose modules really do take several cables of the same kind -- a mixer sums, a multiple splits. Everything else takes one cable per jack, which is Rack's own rule and the reason a feedback loop is summed rather than double-patched.

`transparent` marks a role a signal passes THROUGH without becoming a different kind of thing: a multiple copies it, an attenuator scales it, a slew smooths it. A requirement is satisfied through a chain of these, because 'the random voltage reaches the envelope's time' is just as true when it goes via a mult -- which is how people actually patch. Without this the checker rejects correct patches for being tidy.

oscillator.is: something that makes a repeating waveform

audio_oscillator.is: an oscillator running fast enough to hear as pitch

lfo.is: an oscillator running below hearing, used to move something

filter.is: something that removes part of the spectrum

amplifier.is: something that controls how loud a signal is

envelope.is: a one-shot shape, triggered rather than free-running

function_generator.is: an envelope that can also cycle, slew and respond to voltage

sequencer.is: something that steps through values in order

random.is: a source of values nobody chose

sample_and_hold.is: something that takes a value on a trigger and holds it

noise.is: broadband noise, the raw material for random and for texture

clock.is: a steady pulse everything else times against

clock_modulator.is: something that divides, multiplies or shifts a clock

mixer.$comment: Transparent: a signal through a mixer is still that signal. An oscillator reaching a filter by way of a mixer is how anybody patches two oscillators into one filter, and it was read as never reaching the filter at all.

attenuator.is: something that scales a voltage, often through zero

multiple.is: a splitter, so one signal can reach several places

slew.is: something that slows how fast a voltage may change

waveshaper.is: something that adds harmonics by bending the waveform

delay.is: something that repeats a signal later

reverb.is: something that adds a space around a signal

effect.is: something that processes audio for character rather than level

switch.is: something that routes one of several signals

logic.is: something that combines gates by rule

quantizer.$comment: Transparent: a quantizer snaps a pitch voltage and passes it on, so a register reaching a pitch input THROUGH one still reaches it -- and quantized-voice requires a quantizer in exactly that path.
quantizer.is: something that snaps a voltage to a scale

output.is: the way out of the rack — an audio interface or recorder

gate_out.$comment: SQR and PLS are here because a square or pulse output IS a gate signal -- driving an envelope's trigger from an LFO's square is how a drum gets fired, and leaving them out made the kick drum unsatisfiable with the only clock modules anybody has. not_ports keeps that from reading an OSCILLATOR's pulse as a clock: same label, audio rate, and it would retrigger an envelope thousands of times a second.

cv_in.$comment: Pitch is here because a V/OCT jack is a control-voltage input -- an envelope sweeping an oscillator's pitch lands on it. Our manifests call that jack Pitch and the vendor inference calls it Cv, so a requirement that named only one of them held for Fundamental's VCO and not for ours.
